title: CSS Grid Fundamentals
description: Master 2-dimensional page layouts with CSS Grid: construct explicit grids using grid-template-columns, grid-template-rows, the fr fractional unit, repeat(), and gap.

objectives.statement: Construct explicit 2-dimensional grid layouts using grid-template-columns and grid-template-rows.
Utilize the fr fractional unit and repeat() helper function for responsive column track sizing.

content.title: 2-Dimensional Layout Engineering with CSS Grid
content.hook: While Flexbox excels at 1-dimensional component rows or columns, CSS Grid is designed from the ground up for 2-dimensional page layouts with columns AND rows simultaneously.
content.context: Declaring `display: grid` creates a grid container. Defining `grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr)` establishes three equal-width columns using the flexible `fr` (fraction of free space) unit, while `gap: 1.5rem` creates pristine gutters.
goals: Define explicit column tracks with the `fr` unit.
Use `repeat()` notation for clean, DRY grid definitions.
Place grid items with grid line placement properties.

content.title: CSS Grid Track Lines and Fractional Units
content.description: Grid diagram: Columns defined as 1fr 2fr 1fr divide available space into 4 equal shares (1/4, 2/4, 1/4). Grid lines numbered 1 to 4 bound the column tracks.

content.prompt: A container is 1000px wide with `display: grid; grid-template-columns: 200px 1fr 2fr; gap: 0;`. What are the computed widths of the three column tracks?

feedback.correct: Exact math! First, fixed track 200px is subtracted from 1000px, leaving 800px free space. The 3 total fr shares (1+2=3) divide 800px into 266.6px (1fr) and 533.3px (2fr).
feedback.incorrect: The fr unit distributes *remaining free space*. Subtract fixed 200px from 1000px = 800px. 1fr gets 1/3 of 800px (~266px), 2fr gets 2/3 (~533px).

content.title: Build a 3-Column Dashboard Grid
content.prompt:
Style the `.dashboard-grid` container:
1. Apply `display: grid`.
2. Define 3 equal columns using `grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr)`.
3. Add gutters between cards using `gap: 1.5rem`.
4. Style `.card` with `background-color: #ffffff`, `padding: 1.5rem`, `border: 1px solid #e2e8f0`, and `border-radius: 8px`.

content.prompt: When designing a web interface, how do you decide whether a layout component should use Flexbox or CSS Grid?

feedback.correct: Spot on! Use Flexbox for 1-dimensional component alignment (rows/columns like navigation bars, button groups, icon-text pairs) where content drives sizing. Use CSS Grid for 2-dimensional page layouts (dashboards, article grids, gallery layouts) where layout structure dictates positioning.
feedback.incorrect: Think about 1D (content-driven, single direction) vs 2D (layout-driven, rows and columns simultaneously).

content.title: Key Takeaways: CSS Grid
takeaways: CSS Grid is a 2-dimensional layout engine controlling rows and columns simultaneously.
grid-template-columns defines column tracks using pixels, percentages, or fr units.
The fr fractional unit calculates proportional shares of remaining free space.
repeat(N, track) reduces repetitive track definitions.
The gap property establishes horizontal and vertical gutters between grid cells.
